name: Delivery Gateway for WooCommerce
author: deliverygateway

sections.description:
Delivery Gateway for WooCommerce connects your store to the Delivery Gateway service. It brings delivery configuration, checkout delivery selection, and shipment workflows into WooCommerce.

A Delivery Gateway account and access token are required. Delivery Gateway is an external service. Your use of the service is governed by its own terms and privacy policy.

Features

  • Configure Delivery Gateway providers, fulfillment options, packaging, themes, pickup points, delivery zones, and merchant settings.
  • Add a Delivery Gateway delivery selector to the WooCommerce Checkout Block.
  • Optionally replace WooCommerce’s native shipping selector and synchronize the selected delivery price.
  • Create and review shipments from WooCommerce order screens.
  • Bulk-create shipments for up to 50 selected orders with the bulk shipping workflow.
  • Search for pickup points and set shipment address coordinates with map-based tools.
  • Register shipment webhooks and map Delivery Gateway shipment statuses to WooCommerce order statuses.
  • Optionally disable Cash on Delivery when the selected pickup point does not support it.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.8 or later.
  • WooCommerce installed and active.
  • PHP 8.2 or later.
  • A Delivery Gateway account and API access token.
  • The WooCommerce Checkout Block for the embedded checkout delivery selector.

For more information about the service, visit Delivery Gateway.

External Services

This plugin connects to external services to provide its functionality. Review these services and update your site’s privacy notice as appropriate before enabling the plugin.

Delivery Gateway

Delivery Gateway is the core service required by this plugin.

The plugin connects to the configured Delivery Gateway API endpoint, which defaults to https://api.deliverygateway.io/graphql/merchant. It also derives a public GraphQL endpoint and loads the embedded checkout SDK from the same configured API origin. Connections occur when an administrator authenticates or configures the plugin, manages Delivery Gateway catalog data, creates or views shipments, uses bulk shipping, registers a webhook, or when a customer uses the configured checkout delivery selector. WooCommerce order lifecycle events may also synchronize orders to Delivery Gateway after the plugin has been configured.

Data sent may include the access token; site, WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP, operating system, and plugin version information; merchant configuration and uploaded merchant images; cart currency, language, parcel details, and recipient details; order identifiers and timestamps; customer identifiers; billing and shipping names, email addresses, telephone numbers and addresses; pickup-point and delivery selections; payment method and status; order totals; product, shipping, fee, and coupon line data; parcel data; and shipment details. Delivery Gateway may pass the minimum information needed for fulfillment to the delivery provider selected by the merchant.

  • Delivery Gateway Terms and Conditions
  • Delivery Gateway Privacy Policy

Intercom Messenger

The plugin initializes Intercom Messenger on WooCommerce > Delivery Gateway and WooCommerce > Bulk shipping administration screens to provide support chat. When an administrator visits those screens, the Intercom service may receive network and device information and may set browser storage or cookies used by Messenger. Information submitted in a support conversation is sent to Intercom and Delivery Gateway’s support team.

  • Intercom Terms and Policies
  • Intercom Product Privacy Notice

OpenStreetMap and Nominatim

Administration screens that display a location map request map tiles from OpenStreetMap. Address lookup tools send the entered street, city, postal code, country, and optional state to the public Nominatim geocoding service after a complete address has been entered. These requests also expose ordinary request information such as the site’s referrer and the administrator’s IP address to the service provider.

  • OpenStreetMap Foundation Terms of Use
  • OpenStreetMap Foundation Privacy Policy
  • Nominatim Usage Policy
  • OpenStreetMap Tile Usage Policy

Sentry

Sentry integration is optional and inactive until an administrator provides a Sentry DSN. When enabled, the plugin may send error messages, stack traces, plugin and platform versions, environment type, site URL, the current WordPress user’s ID, username and email address, and diagnostic context to the Sentry project identified by that DSN. The plugin filters known credential fields from event extras, but administrators should review their diagnostic data and Sentry configuration before enabling this feature.

The applicable Terms of Service and Privacy Policy depend on your Sentry project and account configuration.

Privacy

This plugin processes WooCommerce customer, cart, order, payment, delivery, pickup-point, parcel, and shipment information to provide delivery selection and fulfillment features. When configured, relevant data is transmitted to Delivery Gateway and may be shared with the merchant’s selected delivery provider.

Site administrators are responsible for determining a lawful basis for this processing, entering into any required data-processing agreements, disclosing the processing and external services in their customer-facing privacy notice, and responding to data-subject requests. The plugin does not currently add suggested privacy-policy text to WordPress automatically and does not automatically erase its stored data during uninstall.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/delivery-gateway-for-woocommerce, or install the plugin through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate Delivery Gateway for WooCommerce. WooCommerce must already be installed and active.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Delivery Gateway.
  4. Enter the Delivery Gateway API URL and access token supplied for your account, then save the settings.
  5. Complete the onboarding steps and configure providers, packaging, pickup points, zones, and checkout behavior as needed.
  6. To automate order status changes, open the Automations tab, register the webhook, configure the desired mappings, and enable the feature.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Delivery Gateway account?

Yes. The plugin is a connector for the Delivery Gateway service and needs a valid API access token.

Does the plugin work without WooCommerce?

No. WooCommerce is a required plugin.

Does the checkout selector support the classic checkout?

The embedded selector is implemented for the WooCommerce Checkout Block. The order-management and shipment tools are available independently of that storefront selector.

Does the plugin support HPOS?

Yes. The order shipment panel supports both legacy WooCommerce order screens and High-Performance Order Storage screens.
sections.changelog:
0.2.2

  • Initial WordPress.org release.
  • Added Delivery Gateway onboarding and merchant configuration.
  • Added Checkout Block delivery selection and configurable native-selector replacement.
  • Added individual and bulk shipment creation.
  • Added provider, packaging, theme, pickup-point, and delivery-zone management.
  • Added shipment-status webhook automations.
